claims.text: The baseline is a FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy coating deposited on a steel substrate.
The baseline coating has moderate short-range order under standard deposition conditions.
Changing the deposition heat treatment, such as by faster quenching or an altered temperature profile, will reduce short-range ordering relative to the baseline.
The proposed wear behavior applies at sliding temperatures above approximately 600 °C.
Short-range ordering is stable in the FeNiCrCoCu coating at elevated temperature.
Short-range order creates localized obstacles to dislocation glide during high-temperature sliding.
The SRO-induced obstacles reduce plastic flow during sliding.
The SRO-induced obstacles reduce microcrack propagation during sliding.
Reducing short-range order will increase dislocation activity.
Reducing short-range order will increase microscopic plastic deformation.
Reducing short-range order will increase the coating wear rate.
Reducing short-range order will produce more noticeable subsurface damage.
The moderate-SRO baseline has a lower high-temperature wear rate than the reduced-SRO coating.
The moderate-SRO baseline undergoes less microscopic deformation than the reduced-SRO coating at high temperature.
Below or far above the proposed temperature regime, mechanisms such as diffusion-driven softening may dominate wear and deformation.
A comparison at 650–700 °C under identical load and speed can test the predicted directional effects of reduced SRO.
Failure of the reduced-SRO coating to show either increased wear rate or greater dislocation activity relative to the baseline would falsify the proposed controlling role of SRO.
